decisions.rationale: Decided: Firstmate decision react-forms-loop3-correction (inbox 015, 2026-11-18) authorized the third correction loop and the reconciler's full plan, steps 1-10, including both onSave variants. It ruled that matching on the normalized resolved module identity is permitted, because that observes which runtime module loaded, not the learner's import syntax or source shape. Implemented at commit 8543f338 (8543f33893a96e53750774e465c48109b61b67de); current lab.json sha256 4e1b30b6.... The loop-4 education and SME rechecks mark this finding resolved. Verified in tests/verify-learner-test.mjs: Vitest is spawned as process.execPath with tests/node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs, cwd tests/, with no shell and no .cmd shim. A spawn error is printed before exit. Pointing the entry at a missing file now exits 1 with Node's 'Cannot find module' error, not silently. tests/vitest.mutation.config.js compares paths with backslashes converted to forward slashes, and case-folded on win32. Windows was still not run; the claim is resolved by construction from the cited Node and Vite sources. The reconciler checked this independently in a fresh 0700 scratch copy, made with git archive of 8543f338 and the private overlay, on macOS, Node 24.2.0 and npm 11. Accepted with exit 0 and the Task 8 line: the reference test; the reconciler's own complete test; that test with an extensionless import, with an import through ../src, split into two tests without its own cleanup, followed by a test.todo, followed by a second passing test, or writing a raw line to process.stdout; and the complete test against a form whose name input has no type attribute. Rejected with exit 1, the summary still showing 8 passed, and one line per missed behaviour: the TEAMS, firstChild-tag, TASK8_VARIANT and expect(true) vacuous tests; the partial TEAMS-driven test; blank-only; valid-only; and the scenario without onSave assertions. The shipped starter fails all 8. Original loop-3 reconciliation (escalated; recorded at e0daff84 against lab.json sha256 314393f8...): Claim verified true, consolidated with sme-fcc-t1 (and its importer-path half with sme-fcc-t2). Evidence, from official sources retrieved 2026-11-18: the Node April 2024 security release notes for CVE-2024-27980 say spawn and spawnSync now error with EINVAL when a .bat or .cmd file is passed without the shell option. The child_process docs say .bat and .cmd files are not executable without a terminal. The Node source at v22.12.0 (process_wrap.cc and spawn_sync.cc) and at v24.0.0 (spawn_sync.cc) returns UV_EINVAL from IsWindowsBatchFile, so both declared Node lines carry the guard. verify-learner-test.mjs spawns node_modules/.bin/vitest.cmd on win32 without a shell, so on Windows every run fails before Vitest starts. Reproduced on macOS with the .bin path pointed at a missing file: the script exits 1 with no output at all, because it never prints spawnSync's error. The Vite plugin docs (v6.4.6, Path Normalization) say resolved ids use POSIX separators on Windows. The mutation config compares the importer against a raw path.resolve result, which has backslashes on Windows, so that comparison would never match there. Fix direction (plan step 1): spawn process.execPath with tests/node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs (vitest's own package bin entry), with cwd set to tests/; that needs no shell and no .cmd on any OS. Print the spawn error before exiting. Plan step 2 removes the raw path comparison. Until a Windows run is recorded, the solved-run evidence must list Windows as unverified. Feasibility: the reconciler prototyped the whole consolidated fix (plan steps 1-6, tests/ only, setup.js included) in a 0700 scratch copy of b3609592 with the private overlay, on macOS, Node 24 and npm 11. The reference test, and the reconciler's own complete test with the shipped import, are accepted. So are that test with an extensionless import, with an import through ../src, split into two tests (with or without its own cleanup), followed by a test.todo, followed by a second passing test, or writing a raw line to process.stdout. The complete test is also accepted against a form whose name input has no type attribute. Rejected, each with a message naming the missed behaviour: the TEAMS, firstChild-tag and TASK8_VARIANT vacuous tests; the partial TEAMS-driven test; expect(true).toBe(true); blank-only; valid-only; and the README scenario without onSave assertions. The shipped starter still fails all 8 named tests, and the oracle does not run. Windows was not exercised and remains unverified. Consolidated plan: (1) runner portability and diagnostics; (2) resolved-module swap; (3) variants with no footprint; (4) a no-fault control run; (5) any-failure scoring plus shared cleanup; (6) onSave variants; (7) honest disclosure; (8) completion criterion; (9) matcher hints; (10) re-record the solved run and lock, then critic rechecks. Correction-loop status: this lab already ran correction loop 1 (findings edu-fcc-1..9 and sme-fcc-1..5, implemented at 89064f80) and correction loop 2 (findings edu-fcc-r1, edu-fcc-r2, sme-fcc-r1, sme-fcc-r2, implemented at 30cd7583). The Task 8 oracle commits 5b3807c4, 6ba668b6 and b3609592 were the Firstmate-required change that these loop-3 critics rechecked. Implementing this fix changes lab bytes again. That is a third correction loop, or a fourth if the Firstmate-required Task 8 change is counted; either way it exceeds the allowance. authoring/docs/workflow.md section 2.4 allows a second loop once and says a third escalates. This decision is therefore 'escalate': the claim is verified true and the fix direction below is recommended, but the author must not edit any lab byte until Firstmate authorizes the third loop.

The 'completed submission ignored' message points at the onSave-received check, which is consistent with error-gone not being independently scored. The ui-tests topic.json reason matches. The shipped starter fails all 8. Original loop-3 reconciliation (escalated; recorded at e0daff84 against lab.json sha256 314393f8...): Claim verified true. Reproduced at b3609592 with the private overlay: (a) a test that never uses getByRole, getByLabelText, user-event or a findBy/queryBy query is accepted. It uses fireEvent and container lookups but still checks that the error appears and then disappears. (b) A test that follows the README scenario but makes no onSave assertion is also accepted. The diff removed the earlier honest disclosure, and the new README and lab.json wording ('an always-passing or partial test does not earn credit', 'rejecting vacuous and partial tests') over-claims. Part (b) is a contract gap, not only a wording gap: the README's own named scenario includes 'onSave remains uncalled' and 'onSave receives the entered values', so a test without them is partial. Recommended fix (plan step 6), chosen over narrowing the scenario: add two prop-level runtime variants. In one, the wrapper also calls onSave when the name is blank. The reconciler's prototype rejects the no-onSave test with a message naming each missed onSave check. Part (a) cannot be scored without inspecting source or call shape, which the firstmate contract forbids, so it needs disclosure only (plan step 7). Restore in lab.json cleanup.notes and the README task 8 text that the suite proves the test notices each faulty submission behaviour. Querying by role and label, user-event and the getBy/queryBy/findBy choice are self-checked practice and not machine-verified. State exactly which checks the suite scores. With plan step 6 it scores four: the error appears after the blank submission, onSave stays uncalled for the blank submission, the completed resubmission is handled (caught by either the error-gone check or the onSave-received check), and onSave receives the values. The reconciler confirmed with one more probe that 'the error is gone' is not independently scored: the complete test minus its queryBy absence check is still accepted, because the onSave-received check alone catches the 'successful' variant. So list the error-gone check as self-checked. The other option is a stale-error variant, in which the completed submission saves but the earlier error stays visible; that direction is unverified. Define 'partial' only in terms of the scored checks, or drop the word. The 'successful' variant's message should say 'check that the error is gone or that onSave receives the values', not error-gone alone. The uncommitted ui-tests topic.json reason already says the query choice is self-checked, so the two texts would then agree.
